title: Tower Saucer Transparent Play Economy and Amusement Resort Framework

inspiration_sources: Tower Unite social hub and condo economy
Final Fantasy VII Gold Saucer amusement economy
generated_context.core_pitch: A real-world social resort network where guests play games, visit attractions, generate transparent activity data, earn internal reward currency, spend that currency on goods and experiences, and carry their wallet, preferences, room layout, and identity across multiple tower locations.
generated_context.one_line_translation: The funhouse where your data pays you back.

core_definition.summary: The Tower Saucer system is a real-world amusement resort and social hub built around a transparent closed-loop economy. Guests generate data by playing minigames, visiting attractions, interacting with branded products, decorating personal spaces, and participating in events. The system rewards guests with internal Units while making data collection visible, reviewable, and part of the experience rather than a hidden extraction layer.
core_definition.governing_rule: Guest enjoyment, consent, transparency, and agency must remain superior to extraction, compulsion, opaque surveillance, or disguised gambling.

core_separation.reward_equation: guest_value = play + enjoyment + participation + skill + brand_interaction + social_contribution + feedback
core_separation.one_line_translation: If the guest creates value, the guest sees the value trail and receives a transparent reward share.

system_principles.name: Enjoyment First
system_principles.rule: Maximizing guest enjoyment is the top priority while the guest remains in the tower.

system_principles.name: Transparent Data Value
system_principles.rule: Data collection is not hidden; it is openly disclosed, shown to the guest, and framed as part of the reward economy.

system_principles.name: Closed-Loop Currency
system_principles.rule: Units are internal resort currency and should not function as cash unless the system is prepared for banking, gambling, tax, and money-transmission regulation.

system_principles.name: Agency-Preserving Personalization
system_principles.rule: The system may recommend activities, room layouts, prizes, and experiences, but the guest retains final choice.

system_principles.name: No Hidden Extraction
system_principles.rule: Guests must be able to see what data is collected, how it produces value, and how it affects rewards.

system_principles.name: Portable Home Feeling
system_principles.rule: Wallet, room layout, preferences, inventory, and profile state can travel across tower locations.

system_principles.name: Local Uniqueness
system_principles.rule: Different tower locations may offer unique activities, prizes, collectibles, food, and regional reward loops.

system_principles.name: Entertainment Not Entrapment
system_principles.rule: The tower must not optimize for addiction, regret spending, concealed compulsion, or trapped attention.

core_loop.compact_flow: enter -> play -> generate data -> earn Units -> review dashboard -> spend/redeem/customize -> sync -> return or transfer

arcade_tokens.boundary: Tokens are play access, not money.

tickets.boundary: Tickets should reward play and skill without becoming cash-equivalent gambling payout.

prestige_badges.boundary: Prestige cannot be purchased; it represents earned participation or achievement.

local_marks.example: Yukon tower guests may earn local marks through gold-panning challenges and redeem them toward Yukon-exclusive prizes.

brand_credits.boundary: Brand interaction must be disclosed and opt-in where required.

data_model.data_policy_summary: Data collection is a visible feature, not a hidden background extraction. Guests can access their activity logs, reward calculations, brand interactions, and privacy settings during their stay.

guest_profile_system.core_experience: The guest can travel to another tower and feel like their personal space, profile, and earned value came with them.

districts.name: Plaza District
districts.function: Central social hub, orientation area, guest services, public events, shops, and tower navigation.

districts.name: Arcade District
districts.function: Skill games, redemption machines, ticket prizes, rhythm games, claw machines, and sponsor arcade events.

districts.name: Casino District
districts.function: Units-only entertainment gambling area with strict non-cash boundaries and responsible play controls.

districts.name: Horror District
districts.function: Haunted houses, ghost hunts, scare mazes, horror escape rooms, and seasonal fear events.

districts.name: Midway District
districts.function: Carnival-style games, fast play loops, sponsor prizes, and low-barrier casual competition.

districts.name: Ride District
districts.function: Thrill rides, dark rides, simulators, gondolas, indoor coasters, and motion attractions.

districts.name: Adventure District
districts.function: Escape rooms, puzzle adventures, obstacle courses, climbing challenges, and co-op missions.

districts.name: Show District
districts.function: Live performances, tournaments, comedy, magic, esports, trivia finals, and staged events.

districts.name: Market District
districts.function: Shopping, prize redemption, brand stores, local goods, food, souvenirs, and sponsor experiences.

districts.name: Residence District
districts.function: Guest rooms, condo-like personal spaces, furniture layout, trophy display, comfort settings, and transferable home identity.

districts.name: Transit Hub
districts.function: Transfers between towers, luggage support, profile migration, transport credits, and continuity services.

haunted_house_model.summary: A high-replay attraction type that combines story, fear, exploration, co-op behavior, and seasonal rewards.
haunted_house_model.disclosure_template: This attraction tracks route decisions, reaction timing, teamwork behavior, and fear-response choices to improve future horror experiences.

dark_ride_model.summary: Ride-through attraction with branching scenes, scoring, hidden objects, and regional story themes.

escape_room_model.summary: Skill-based solo or co-op puzzle attraction that rewards completion, speed, low hint use, and teamwork.

seasonal_event_model.summary: Rotating limited-time attractions keep towers alive and encourage repeat visits.

location_exclusive_system.purpose: Make each tower location worth visiting by tying activities and prizes to local geography, culture, industry, climate, and myth.

room_and_furniture_system.summary: Guest rooms function as portable personal spaces and trophy displays. Furniture arrangement is entirely controlled by the guest.

brand_product_placement_model.summary: Branded clothing and products worn or used inside the tower can function as product placement or advertising interaction, but must be disclosed and counted toward guest data-generation value.

background_simulation.purpose: Maintain economic balance, attraction quality, reward availability, guest flow, and cross-location continuity.

legal_and_ethics_boundaries.general_note: This framework is conceptual and requires jurisdiction-specific legal review before real-world deployment.

failure_modes.name: Hidden Extraction Drift
failure_modes.description: The tower claims transparency but begins collecting or monetizing data in ways guests cannot see or understand.
failure_modes.countermeasure: Guest-visible data dashboard, plain-language disclosures, audit logs, and opt-out controls.

failure_modes.name: Disguised Gambling Collapse
failure_modes.description: Units, casino games, and valuable prizes combine into a structure regulators or guests experience as gambling with cash-equivalent value.
failure_modes.countermeasure: No cashout, separate casino units, visible odds, capped winnings, age controls, and legal review.

failure_modes.name: Fun Turns Into Work
failure_modes.description: Guests begin to feel they are laboring for data rewards rather than enjoying a resort.
failure_modes.countermeasure: Optimize for satisfaction after leaving, not just activity volume or dwell time.

failure_modes.name: Unit Inflation
failure_modes.description: Too many Units are issued, causing prices to rise or rewards to lose meaning.
failure_modes.countermeasure: Balanced reward rates, meaningful currency sinks, event caps, and economic simulation.

failure_modes.name: Pay-To-Win Status Corruption
failure_modes.description: Purchased currency starts replacing earned achievement, damaging the prestige system.
failure_modes.countermeasure: Separate purchased convenience from earned badges, milestones, and exclusive achievements.

failure_modes.name: Brand Creep
failure_modes.description: Sponsored products become too intrusive and guests feel like the tower is an ad trap.
failure_modes.countermeasure: Disclosure, opt-in campaigns, reward clarity, brand-light zones, and sponsor caps.

failure_modes.name: Personalization Becomes Control
failure_modes.description: The system begins steering guests toward operator profit instead of guest enjoyment.
failure_modes.countermeasure: Guest agency controls, transparent recommendations, preference editing, and no hidden manipulation.

failure_modes.name: Transfer Identity Fragility
failure_modes.description: Guests expect continuity between towers, but missing inventory, room mismatch, or wallet errors break trust.
failure_modes.countermeasure: Strong synchronization, transfer previews, rollback logs, and manual guest support.

distortion_tests.name: Transparency Test
distortion_tests.question: Can the guest see what data was collected and how it affected rewards?

distortion_tests.name: Enjoyment Test
distortion_tests.question: Does the system optimize for the guest leaving satisfied rather than merely staying longer or spending more?

distortion_tests.name: Cashout Test
distortion_tests.question: Can Units become cash or cash-equivalent value in a way that changes the legal category of the system?

distortion_tests.name: Consent Test
distortion_tests.question: Did the guest knowingly agree to the data use, brand interaction, or activity risk?

distortion_tests.name: Agency Test
distortion_tests.question: Can the guest refuse, opt out, leave, or choose differently without being unfairly punished?

distortion_tests.name: Reward Integrity Test
distortion_tests.question: Are rewards tied to clear activity, skill, participation, or disclosed value generation?

distortion_tests.name: Gambling Boundary Test
distortion_tests.question: Does any casino or chance system create real-money risk or cash-equivalent payout?

distortion_tests.name: Local Value Test
distortion_tests.question: Does the location-exclusive reward actually reflect the place, or is it generic scarcity dressed as tourism?

sequence.description: Guest arrives, loads Tower Passport, sees wallet, privacy settings, room layout, and suggested activities.
Guest reviews data dashboard explanation and chooses data-sharing level.
Guest plays a minigame, earns Units based on participation, performance, and feedback.
Guest converts some Units into Arcade Tokens, earns Tickets, and redeems a small prize.
Guest completes a scare maze, earns a bravery badge and haunted furniture blueprint.
Guest spends Units on food and optionally interacts with a disclosed sponsor product.
Guest places newly unlocked haunted furniture in their room and saves the layout.
Guest checks what value they generated and how rewards were calculated.
Guest books another tower and chooses to replicate their room layout and carry wallet balance forward.

sample_location_package.local_equation: Yukon identity + gold challenge + haunted mine + northern lights reward set = location-exclusive tourism loop

psc_summary.clean_formula: transparent_tower_value = fun + consent + data_visibility + reward_share + portable_identity + local_exclusivity
psc_summary.anti_formula: bad_tower_value = hidden_tracking + compulsion + disguised_gambling + opaque_rewards + loss_of_agency
psc_summary.final_translation: A Tower works when it feels like a place guests choose to return to, not a machine that quietly extracts from them.
